A1.justification: Both readable 10-page PDFs describe the same EmoEdit work, with corresponding equations, figures, tables and references. Neither contains an appendix. Both reference supplementary material absent from the supplied files; this comparison covers the supplied contents.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-editing evaluations in Table 1, a 41-participant user study in Table 2, and qualitative ablations and application results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original quantitative evaluations, user-study outcomes, ablations and application results reported in v2.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same emotion-factor data construction, Q-Former-based Emotion adapter, instruction and diffusion losses, and training and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both use the same 40,120-pair EmoEditSet, 405-image inference set and eight target emotions. The editing and stylized-generation applications also retain identical coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains SDEdit, PnP, InsDiff, P2P-Zero, ControlNet, BlipDiff, CLVA and AIF. Table 2 retains SDEdit, P2P-Zero and BlipDiff as user-study comparators; qualitative comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Both evaluate 3,240 image-emotion pairs using the same six metrics. The user study retains 41 participants, 40 image sets and the same three preference questions. No reported experimental settings change.

E4.justification: The adapter and loss ablations in Figure 6, guidance-scale analysis in Figure 7, and adapter-transfer demonstrations in Figures 8–9 are identical.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains identical percentage and plus/minus reporting. Neither version adds or changes run counts, seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedures or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative examples are unchanged. EmoEdit retains 50.09% Emo-A and 0.335 Emo-S in Table 1, and 89.12% balance preference in Table 2.

T1.justification: The attention equations and loss definitions in Equations 1–4 are identical. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about content-aware affective editing, EmoEditSet, the portable Emotion adapter and its empirical advantages.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are identical, including the emotion-versus-structure tradeoff, restricted emotion factors and categories, dependence on EmoSet, and potential evaluation bias.

D1.justification: Data-filtering thresholds, construction instructions, frozen/trainable model descriptions and data-source links are unchanged. v3 supplies no additional implementation or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research-positioning statements and all 54 reference entries are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first affiliation changes from 'Shenzhen University' to 'CSSE, Shenzhen University,' and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded affiliation is recentered and the updated first-page margin stamp is slightly repositioned. Figures 1–9, Tables 1–2 and their captions are unchanged; pages 2–10 render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 only clarifies an affiliation and updates first-page metadata and placement. The scientific content, evidence, explanations and reproducibility information remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
